decisive_items: progressively worsening sharp epigastric pain radiating to the back of one-day duration
No acute abnormality of the pancreas
response.rationale: Acute pancreatitis is supported by typical epigastric pain radiating to back, nausea/vomiting, and markedly elevated lipase; CT can be normal early. Chronic pancreatitis (R1) is contradicted by acute onset and normal pancreas on CT. Other candidates lack key diagnostic features or are secondary findings.

rejected.why: No ketosis or acidosis data; diabetes is background, not acute cause.
No imaging or exam evidence of obstruction; pain pattern more pancreatic.
Hypertension and CKD are chronic; no renal artery imaging or bruit.
BP elevated but no acute target-organ damage beyond pain; pain not explained.
Dehydration is a consequence, not primary diagnosis.
CKD is chronic history, not acute presentation.
Same as R3; no hypertensive emergency criteria.
No ulcer history, no bleeding, pain radiates to back; lipase elevation not explained.
No cardiac risk factor acute change, ECG/troponin absent; abdominal tenderness points away.
Acute onset and normal pancreas contradict chronic pancreatitis.
